modes.cue_notes: Lie on the belly and prop up on one forearm (or both in a Sphinx position). Bend one knee and bring the heel toward the same-side buttock. Use the same-side hand to hold the ankle and gently draw it toward the glute, creating a quadriceps stretch. Keep the hip of the bent leg on the floor. The other leg extends straight behind. Hold each side.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: Targets the anterior thigh (quadriceps, rectus femoris) and hip flexors. The stomach meridian runs along the anterior thigh; kidney lines the lumbar area. A more accessible alternative before full Frog.

breathing_cues.entering: From a prone or Sphinx position, inhale. On your exhale, bend one knee and slowly draw the heel toward the glute, pausing if you feel any sharp sensation in the knee or thigh. Allow the hip to remain grounded as you settle into the shape.
breathing_cues.holding: Breathe steadily and direct attention to the front of the bent-leg thigh. Each exhale is an invitation for the quadriceps fascia to release; do not pull harder on the ankle; let the breath do the releasing. If the lumbar feels compressed, soften the supporting forearm and allow the chest to drop slightly.
breathing_cues.exiting: On an inhale, release the grip on the ankle and slowly extend the bent leg back to the floor. Exhale and rest in Crocodile or transition directly to the second side.

modifications.name: Reduced Knee Flexion
modifications.description: Rather than drawing the heel fully toward the glute, stop at whatever angle is comfortable for the knee. Use a strap around the ankle instead of the hand to avoid over-pulling.

modifications.name: Bolster Under Hip
modifications.description: Place a bolster or folded blanket under the hip of the bent-leg side to prevent the pelvis from tilting and rotating, keeping the stretch more symmetrical and reducing lumbar strain.

modifications.name: Prop Under Ankle
modifications.description: Place a block or rolled blanket under the ankle of the bent leg to reduce the angle of dorsiflexion and relieve pressure on the ankle joint, suitable for ankle sensitivity.

modifications.name: Double Forearm Support
modifications.description: Instead of using one hand to hold the ankle, prop up on both forearms (Sphinx position) and use a strap around the ankle so both arms are free for balanced support, reducing torso rotation.

emotional_release_potential.notes: The stomach meridian runs along the anterior thigh, the primary tissue targeted here. Stored frustration, undigested experiences, and rumination associated with the stomach organ can arise during sustained holds.

The intensity of the quadriceps stretch and the bilateral asymmetry of the pose can activate the liver's tendency toward holding and needing to control outcomes. Release here is also a release of control.
